items.proposal: S2 finding S2-N1 (major, not a blocker), re-measured by the orchestrator (MEASURED, e3_evidence/s2_measure.json: a whole-row search for the seven tier words): 14 of 75 rows carry no provenance tier word in any field: W1-002, W1-003, W1-004, W1-005, W1-006, W1-007, W1-008, W1-009, W1-010, W1-011, W1-012, W1-013, W2-007, W4-011. Strategy section 8 item 7: every count and claim carries its tier. No E1 or E2 ruling covers it and no suite member tests it (REPORTED by S2). Which claims in each row need a tier is a reading judgment the orchestrator has not made. Proposal A: order FIXUP-3 for W1, W2 and W4 (three lanes at most): in exactly these rows the author adds the tier word (and, per the strategy, the file for EXTRACTED or the script for MEASURED) to each count and claim already in the row, and changes no claim, no boundary, no quotation and no other row; a claim the author cannot support from the pinned bytes is tiered INFERRED, never deleted. Proposal B: no fix-up; the primaries review the rows as they stand with this finding attached, and it goes to the end review. Say which, and if A, name per part the rows and fields in scope.

S2 finding S2-N2 (minor), re-measured (MEASURED, same file): the word 'Fable' names a reviewer role in row prose at W1-004.device_notes, W1-009.device_notes, W1-010.strongest_rejected_alternative, where W2 and W6 write 'the end review'. The role_tokens member is GREEN and does not test this word (REPORTED by S2). Proposal: if W1 is opened for S2-N1, the same author replaces the role name with 'the end review' in exactly these three fields, changing nothing else in each sentence; if W1 is not opened, route to the end review with no row change.

S2 REPORTS that all 137 triage flags fall in W3 (8) and W4 (129), so its 22 hand-read dispositions cover two parts where the S2 brief asked for four, and that the triage members say nothing about W1, W2, W5 or W6. Proposal: accept the two-part coverage as the most the flags allow; note for the primaries that an empty flag list on four parts is not evidence about their prose.

S2 REPORTS that the FIXUP-2 W2 change records name boundary_evidence_refs without an entry index and that FIXUP-1 W4 has two entries sharing one 'before' text, so neither replays mechanically, while the applied bytes are right by S2's own diff. Proposal: no row change; the orchestrator records it in the close record, and any FIXUP-3 order requires each change record to carry the entry index and a unique 'before'.

If you order FIXUP-3: what must hold before the primaries launch. Proposal: no further S-review. The orchestrator applies the changes, then MEASURES and installs by receipt: (1) a diff showing every changed field lies in an ordered row and field; (2) for S2-N1 rows, that the text with the added tier words (and their file or script names) removed equals the text before; (3) the suite hard GREEN with no dead member and tiling GREEN on the applied rows; (4) CWO-DAN-01..04 re-swept with coverage; (5) every new flag triaged; (6) zero rows without a tier word and zero 'Fable' in row prose. Any check that fails comes back to you. Alternative: a full S3 review. The two blind primaries read all 75 rows in either case.

Proposal: fixup3_may_launch and fixup3_parts as your rulings open them; primaries_may_launch true only when the AFTER-FIXUP3 conditions you set are met and recorded by receipt (or true on this ruling if you choose Proposal B for S2-N1). The eight E2 s2_conditions were REPORTED met by S2.
